newsitem.title: USA: Ecuador Finmin refuses to comment on resignation.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador Finmin refuses to comment on resignation.

text.p: Ecuadorean Finance Minister Carlos Davalos on Friday declined to comment on his recent offer to resign from his job.

Davalos, who tendered his resignation to President Fabian Alarcon this week, declined to answer a reporter's questions as he was whisked away from the International Monetary Fund headquarters, where he had been attending meetings.
Two other members of Ecuador's economic team, Central Bank General Manager Fidel Jaramillo and Monetary Board President Danilo Carrera, said they were not quitting.
Washington-based Ecuadorean officials declined to comment on Davalos' possible exit, limiting themselves to stating that the decision was in Alarcon's hands.
Jaramillo, who got into the same car as Davalos, responded to a question on whether he too was resigning with a curt, "No, there's nothing on that score."
Carrera, who left the IMF building separately, also denied he would resign.

The economic team's one-day visit to Washington took place amid rumors of a rift between politicians and technocrats in Alarcon's interim administration. On Thursday, Ecuador PDI bonds dropped 1-3/8 dollars to 64-3/4 dollars on news of Davalos' offer to resign.

The Ecuadorean economic team, which took office after populist President Abdala Bucaram was ousted by Congress in February, said in March that it wanted to reach a standby program with the IMF. One of Ecuador's main challenges is to close a massive fiscal deficit, which stands close to five percent of its gross domestic product.
